title: Prom and Homecoming
premise: Ulyana Brightwater has survived being the only out kid in Millbrook, population nine hundred, by perfecting the art of invisibility. But when a group chat she never joined starts posting messages that predict disasters hours before they happen, Ulyana and five classmates realize they're bound to something that wants to be witnessed — and it's counting down to graduation night. To break the cycle, they must win two championships: the basketball title nobody in town cares about, and a stranger, older contest called Homecoming Court that decides who the town remembers. In the end, Ulyana wins neither crown but breaks the prediction by choosing visibility over victory, sacrificing her own memory of the year so her friends can keep theirs.
about_author: Sable Sandoval grew up in a farming town small enough that everyone knew everyone's business, which is where they learned that secrets are just stories waiting for an audience. They now write from a converted grain silo office, specializing in queer small-town YA with a supernatural edge.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred People, One Closet Door
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She navigates another anonymous day at Millbrook High, cataloging every microaggression with practiced numbness while secretly pining for Delia Marsh, the debate captain. The emotional beat is weary self-protection: Ulyana insists to herself that invisible equals safe, setting up everything she'll lose.

chapters.title: The Chat Nobody Made
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A group chat named 'prom committee' appears on her phone with five other students she barely knows, announcing that the water tower will collapse Friday. It does. The beat is vertigo — the first crack in her controlled, forgettable life, and the first time anyone looks directly at her.

chapters.title: Five Strangers and a Prophecy
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs introduce the chat members: Marcus (quarterback hiding anxiety), Priya (valedictorian), twins Sam and Jo (farm kids), and Delia. They compare screenshots and realize none of them created the group. The beat is uneasy alliance — six people who've spent years ignoring each other now share one secret.

chapters.title: Rules of the Game
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. The chat posts its second prediction, this time naming a student's injury, and includes instructions: 'Win what doesn't matter. Then win what does.' The group deciphers it as the basketball championship and Homecoming Court. The beat is dread disguised as strategy.

chapters.title: Tryouts
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. He pulls strings to get Ulyana and the others onto the basketball team as managers-then-players, since the prophecy requires them on the roster. Ulyana is terrible; Delia is worse. The beat is humiliating comedy that slowly becomes genuine belonging.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Jo's POV. Researching 'Homecoming Court' in the library archive, Jo finds photos of past courts going back a century — every winner died or vanished within a year of graduation. The beat is horror: the contest isn't tradition, it's a harvest.

chapters.title: First Loss
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. The team loses their first game badly, and the chat punishes them with a prediction that comes true: the diner burns down, empty, but close. The beat is guilt — they're learning the entity rewards effort and punishes apathy.

chapters.title: Delia, Off Script
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Late-night practice becomes an almost-confession between Ulyana and Delia, interrupted when the chat predicts Delia's car crash — and they prevent it by breaking a pattern for the first time. The beat is hope: the future can be fought.

chapters.title: The Winning Streak
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Montage chapter: the team starts winning as the town, starved for anything to celebrate, rallies around them. Ulyana becomes locally famous. The beat is intoxication — visibility feels like love, and love feels safe, which is exactly the trap.

chapters.title: Nominated
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Homecoming nominations post, and all six names appear — though only one can win. Priya calculates the odds and realizes the entity wants them competing against each other. The beat is fracture: friendship curdling into strategy.

chapters.title: Campaign Season
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The school splits into factions; old grudges surface; Sam and Jo fight over campaign tactics. Meanwhile the chat goes quiet, which frightens them more than threats did. The beat is disintegration under pressure.

chapters.title: The Archive Speaks
chapters.summary: Jo's POV. Jo interviews the oldest resident, who remembers 1954, when her sister won Homecoming Queen and was 'remembered out of existence' — forgotten by everyone including her own mother. The beat is revelation: winning means being consumed as memory.

chapters.title: Throwing the Game
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The group plots to lose the semifinal deliberately to avoid the championship the prophecy demands. The chat retaliates instantly with a prediction targeting Jo. The beat is despair — there is no opt-out, only choosing whom to protect.

chapters.title: Semifinal
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Forced to play honestly after the retaliation, they win in overtime. Marcus has a panic attack on the bench and Ulyana covers for him publicly. The beat is solidarity: the team stops being a means to an end and becomes a family.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At prom, Ulyana and Delia finally kiss under the gym lights while the chat posts its most specific prediction yet: 'One of you will be remembered. Choose.' The beat is bittersweet joy — the best night of their lives shadowed by the countdown.

chapters.title: The Fine Print
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Decoding a century of predictions, Priya discovers the loophole: the entity needs a willing winner. Refusal by all six breaks the contract — but the price is that one volunteer must surrender their memories of the year. The beat is terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Championship
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. The final game, played before the whole town. They win 'what doesn't matter,' and the chat responds: 'Now the one that does.' Sam takes a brutal hit protecting Jo, echoing the first prediction. The beat is triumph laced with dread.

chapters.title: Homecoming Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Coronation assembly. As votes are read, each friend publicly refuses the crown in turn, breaking the script — until the entity begins erasing the crowd's memories in real time. The beat is climax chaos: love declared aloud while the world forgets it.

chapters.title: Brightwater
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Understanding someone must pay, Ulyana accepts the crown alone, volunteering her memories of the year — the friends, the team, Delia — to save the rest. The beat is sacrifice: the girl who hid behind invisibility chooses to disappear completely, on purpose, for love.

chapters.title: The Girl Nobody Remembers
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Graduation approaches; everyone has forgotten the events except fragments. Delia finds Ulyana's annotated copy of the archive and realizes what happened. The beat is grief and detective-work: refusing to let the sacrifice be total.

chapters.title: Remember Me Wrong
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia reconstructs the year through artifacts — photos, the chat logs, a prom corsage — and tells Ulyana their story back to her piece by piece. Memory returns not through magic but through witness. The beat is tender persistence: love as an act of retelling.

chapters.title: Prom and Homecoming
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Fully remembered, Ulyana stands up at graduation as class speaker and tells the whole town the truth about the year, the entity, and herself — out loud, unhidden. The chat deletes itself forever. The beat is resolution: survival isn't staying invisible; it's being seen and staying anyway.
